mainTopic: Can a יבם cancel the vows of a שומרת יבם? Testing and supporting רבי אמי's claim that רבי אליעזר means a case where the יבם did מאמר.
overview: Earlier, רבי אמי explained that רבי אליעזר in the משנה, who lets the יבם cancel the vows of a שומרת יבם, is talking about a case where the יבם already did מאמר. The גמרא tests this explanation. First it asks how a woman acquired through מאמר can be called 'acquired from Heaven.' The answer is that he acquired her, but only through the bond Heaven made. Next the גמרא says רבי אמי's reading would solve רבה's question about whether מאמר creates אירוסין or נשואין according to בית שמאי. רב נחמן בר יצחק blocks that proof: 'he cancels' can mean together with her father. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא that supports רבי אמי. In it, רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא argue about one יבם versus two, and רבי עקיבא answers each challenge so well that בן עזאי regrets not having served him. At the end of the amud the גמרא starts asking how this ברייתא supports רבי אמי; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה's wording seems to clash with רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from the משנה. It then challenges רבי אמי: if the יבם did מאמר, he acquired her himself, so she is not a woman acquired 'from Heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה that רבי אליעזר said: A husband can cancel the vows of a wife he acquired himself. So surely he can cancel the vows of a woman Heaven gave him. But if the case is one where the יבם did מאמר, then he did acquire her himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's argument from the משנה. It uses that argument to attack רבי אמי's explanation that the case involves מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's whole argument depends on a contrast: a wife the husband acquired himself versus a woman Heaven gave him. If the יבם already did מאמר, he took an action to acquire her. Then she seems to belong in the first group, and the contrast falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Just as... (opens a קל וחומר)
Cancels her vows
Whom Heaven gave him, meaning the יבמה, who is tied to him automatically
A betrothal the יבם does with the יבמה before יבום

steps.confusionAlert: The 'woman acquired from Heaven' is the יבמה. She becomes tied to the יבם automatically when her husband dies without children. He did nothing to make that happen.

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Just as a woman whom he acquired for himself
he nullifies her vows,
then a woman whom Heaven acquired for him
isn't it logical that he should nullify her vows?
But if it is a case where he performed מאמר with her,
then he acquired her for himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּשֶׁעָשָׂה בָּהּ מַאֲמָר, קָנָה לְעַצְמוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the challenge against רבי אמי's explanation, which came earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that רבי אליעזר's case involves מאמר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once there is מאמר, the יבם acquired her himself. That conflicts with the משנה calling her a woman acquired 'from Heaven.'

steps.title: He acquired her, but only through Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even with מאמר, she is a woman he acquired through Heaven's help.
steps.simpleTranslation: He acquired her for himself, but by means of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אמי. The מאמר was his act, but the only reason he could do it is that Heaven tied her to him first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'acquired from Heaven' does not mean he took no action at all. It means the connection was set up by Heaven, because she fell to him through her husband's death. So רבי אליעזר's contrast still works, even in a מאמר case.

keyTerms.meaning: By means of Heaven, through the bond Heaven created

phrases.english: It is one whom he acquired for himself by means of Heaven.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Acquired from Heaven' means he did nothing at all to acquire her.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Acquired from Heaven' means he acquired her through a bond Heaven made. That fits a מאמר case.

steps.title: רבי אמי's reading would solve רבה's open question
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: if רבי אמי is right, we could solve רבה's famous unsolved question about what מאמר does according to בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could then solve רבה's question: according to בית שמאי, does מאמר create אירוסין or נשואין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge by bringing up רבה's question, which was never answered. This step sets up the next step, where the גמרא will show how רבי אמי's reading would answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the challenge is that רבה's question was left open. If רבי אמי's explanation would settle it so easily, that suggests his explanation may be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: You could solve (an open question)
Asked, raised as a question
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Full marriage

phrases.english: You could resolve that which Rabba asked:
מאמר according to בית שמאי,
does it create betrothal, or does it create full marriage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new one against רבי אמי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading would settle a question that was left unsolved. That makes his reading suspicious.

steps.title: The proof: no father is mentioned, so it must be full marriage
steps.stepSummary: If מאמר created only אירוסין, the father would have to share in cancelling her vows. The משנה mentions only the יבם, so מאמר must create נשואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could prove that it creates נשואין. If it created only אירוסין, we learned that for a betrothed נערה, her father and her husband cancel her vows together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how רבי אמי's reading would solve רבה's question. It points out that the משנה says the יבם alone cancels the vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothed נערה needs both her father and her husband to cancel her vows. In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says only 'he cancels' and does not mention the father. That would mean the מאמר made her fully married.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed girl in the stage of נערות
They cancel (plural)

phrases.english: Resolve that it creates full marriage.
Because if it created only betrothal —
didn't we learn: a betrothed young woman,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on נדרים 66b.

phrases.english: her father and her husband nullify her vows?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from step 3 by giving the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: That מאמר according to בית שמאי creates נשואין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on נדרים 66b about a נערה המאורסה, together with the fact that our משנה does not mention the father

steps.title: 'He cancels' can mean together with the father
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק blocks the proof: when רבי אליעזר says 'he cancels,' it can mean he cancels in partnership with the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'he cancels' mean? He cancels as a partner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that the משנה's silence about the father proves nothing. 'He cancels' can mean the יבם takes part in the cancelling together with the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 4 assumed that 'he cancels' means the יבם cancels alone. Once it can mean 'as a partner with the father,' מאמר may create only אירוסין. So רבה's question stays open, and רבי אמי's reading is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: In partnership, together with someone else
What (does it mean)?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's explanation (that the case involves מאמר) survives both challenges. 'Acquired from Heaven' fits a מאמר case, and 'he cancels' can mean together with the father.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
What is meant by 'he nullifies'?
He nullifies in partnership.
phrases.notes: He means in partnership with her father, just like any betrothed נערה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי יָפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 4, which ends the challenge from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that מאמר creates נשואין, so the challenge to רבי אמי falls away.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'he cancels' means 'alone.' It can mean 'in partnership with the father.'

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא that supports רבי אמי: for a שומרת יבם, whether there is one יבם or two, רבי אליעזר says he cancels, רבי יהושע says only with one, and רבי עקיבא says with neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches like רבי אמי: A שומרת יבם, whether there is one יבם or two. רבי אליעזר says: he cancels. רבי יהושע says: with one, but not with two. רבי עקיבא says: not with one and not with two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that it says supports רבי אמי's explanation. Here it only quotes the ברייתא. Step 12 begins to ask how exactly it supports him, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lays out a three-way dispute and adds a detail the משנה did not have: one יבם versus two. רבי אליעזר lets the יבם cancel even when there are two יבמין. רבי יהושע allows it only with one, and רבי עקיבא never allows it. Where the support for רבי אמי lies is not stated here; the גמרא starts asking about it in step 12, and the answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא), bringing support
A widow waiting for her יבם
Brothers-in-law (more than one יבם)

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the defense of רבי אמי a step further. He did not just survive the challenges; a ברייתא backs him up.

phrases.english: It is also taught so, in line with Rabbi Ami:
A widow awaiting her יבם,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יָבָם אֶחָד בֵּין שְׁנֵי יְבָמִין,
phrases.english: whether one יבם or two יבמין,
Rabbi Eliezer says: he nullifies,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לְאֶחָד וְלֹא לִשְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua says: for one, but not for two.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא לְאֶחָד וְלֹא לִשְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: not for one and not for two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With both challenges answered, the גמרא now brings positive support for רבי אמי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's claim that רבי אליעזר's case involves מאמר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the three-way dispute of רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא about a שומרת יבם

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's logical argument for the יבם's full power
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues with a קל וחומר: if a regular wife, in whom a man has no share before marriage, comes fully under his control once she enters his domain, then surely a יבמה, in whom he already has a share, comes fully under his control once she enters his domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: A regular woman is someone a man has no share in before she comes under his control. Yet once she does come under his control, she is fully his. So a woman he already has a share in before she comes under his control, meaning his יבמה, should surely be fully his once she comes under his control!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר gives a logical proof for his opinion that the יבם can cancel her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'small' case is a regular wife: there is no connection before קידושין, and still she becomes fully his. The 'big' case is a יבמה: there is already a connection from the start. So once she enters his domain, she should become fully his for cancelling vows.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
A share or connection to the woman
His domain or control
She becomes fully his

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִם אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בָּהּ
phrases.english: Just as a woman in whom he has no share
phrases.notes: This is a regular woman he marries through קידושין.

phrases.english: before she comes into his domain,
once she comes into his domain, she is fully his.
A woman in whom he does have a share
phrases.notes: This is his יבמה, who is tied to him as soon as his brother dies.

phrases.english: before she comes into his domain,
once she comes into his domain,
is it not logical that she should be fully his?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה אִם אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's opinion in the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a יבם has full power to cancel his יבמה's vows
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a regular wife

steps.title: רבי עקיבא rejects the argument because others share in a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the קל וחומר fails. A regular wife is acquired by the man himself, and no one else has any share in her. A יבמה is given to him from Heaven, and other brothers have a share in her just like he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: No. You can say this about a woman he acquired by himself, since just as he had no share in her, nobody else had a share in her either. But can you say it about a woman given to him from Heaven, where just as he has a share in her, others also have a share in her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר by showing the two cases are not really comparable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treated the יבם's early 'share' as a plus. רבי עקיבא shows it is actually a weakness: that share is not his alone, because his brothers have it too. A regular wife is fully his own, so the comparison breaks.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired her by himself, through קידושין
She was given to him from Heaven, through יבום
Others, meaning the other brothers

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: No,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁקָּנָה הוּא לְעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: if you say this about a woman he acquired for himself,
since just as he has no share in her,
so too others have no share in her.

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִקְנוּ לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: Will you say it about a woman given to him from Heaven,
where just as he has a share in her,
so too others have a share in her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר of רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The יבם's share is shared with his brothers, unlike a husband's exclusive hold on a regular wife.

steps.title: רבי יהושע asks about the case of only one יבם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע challenges רבי עקיבא: your reason works when there are two יבמין, but what about when there is only one יבם and nobody else shares in her?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Akiva, your words work for two יבמין. What do you answer about one יבם?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי עקיבא's reason by pointing to a case where it does not seem to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reason was that 'others have a share.' With only one יבם, there are no others. This fits רבי יהושע's own view from step 6 that one יבם can cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother who may do יבום with the widow
More than one such brother
Answer or reply

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: Akiva,
your words fit a case of two יבמין,

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַתָּה מֵשִׁיב עַל יָבָם אֶחָד?
phrases.english: what do you answer about one יבם?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרֶיךָ בִּשְׁנֵי יְבָמִין מָה אַתָּה מֵשִׁיב עַל יָבָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי עקיבא gave in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reason that others share in the יבמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With only one יבם, no one else has a share, so the reason falls away.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the laws of יבום never make that distinction
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that in the laws of יבום we never split between one יבם and two, or between when מאמר was done and when it was not. Vows follow the same pattern as all the other laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did we ever make a difference between one יבם and two יבמין, or between when he did מאמר with her and when he did not? Just like the other laws, so too vows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא defends his position by saying the one-יבם case follows the same rule as the two-יבמין case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not try to find 'others' in the one-יבם case. Instead he argues that the halacha treats every יבמה as one category. Since other יבום laws never split these cases, vows should not split either.

keyTerms.meaning: We made a distinction
Rabbinic betrothal done by the יבם before יבום
Other laws
Vows

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did we ever distinguish between one יבם
and two יבמין,
whether he did מאמר with her
or whether he did not do מאמר with her?
And just as with other laws, so too with vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם חִלַּקְנוּ עַל יָבָם אֶחָד וְעַל שְׁנֵי יְבָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uniform category: the halacha does not split cases of יבום
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one יבם, no one else shares in her, so he should be able to cancel.
steps.terutzMaskana: All יבמות are treated alike, so even one יבם cannot cancel her vows.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the יבם cancels. רבי יהושע: only with one יבם. רבי עקיבא: never, because a woman 'from Heaven' is shared, and the halacha treats all יבום cases the same.

steps.title: בן עזאי's regret at not serving רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: After this exchange, בן עזאי said to himself that it was a shame he had not served רבי עקיבא, showing how impressed he was by רבי עקיבא's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said it in these words: Too bad for you, בן עזאי, that you did not serve רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with בן עזאי praising רבי עקיבא's sharp answer by expressing regret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line adds no new halacha. It closes the ברייתא by showing the strength of רבי עקיבא's reasoning in this debate.

keyTerms.meaning: In these words
Too bad for you, what a loss
You served, meaning you attended a teacher to learn from him

phrases.english: In these words בן עזאי said:
Too bad for you, בן עזאי,
phrases.notes: בן עזאי is talking to himself here.

phrases.english: that you did not serve רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲבָל עָלֶיךָ בֶּן עַזַּאי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁימַּשְׁתָּ אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא with a comment on רבי עקיבא's answer in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's reasoning in this debate was so strong that בן עזאי regretted not serving him.

steps.title: The גמרא begins asking how the ברייתא supports רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: With one word, מאי, the גמרא opens a question about how the ברייתא it just quoted supports רבי אמי's explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by opening a question about the ברייתא it just quoted. The rest of the question comes right after this word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was brought to support רבי אמי's explanation. Before accepting that support, the גמרא asks what exactly the connection is. This one word only opens the question; the content of the question follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: What? An Aramaic question word that opens a question.
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
An אמורא whose explanation the ברייתא was brought to support

phrases.english: What

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא ends with בן עזאי's praise of רבי עקיבא, the גמרא turns to ask how this ברייתא connects to רבי אמי's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the quoted ברייתא supports רבי אמי's explanation. The full question is finished in the next words.
